# #137 — Optional: controlled remote qmd deep-lookup wrapper

## Context
The Open Brain / qmd / Hermes memory goal deliberately made qmd optional for normal Hermes memory correctness. qmd runs only on the local GPU Mac today. Durable facts needed by GPU-less agents are promoted into Open Brain and are already usable through hosted OB/mcp2cli.

## Optional Scope
Build a controlled remote qmd wrapper only as a best-effort deep lookup escape hatch after the durable OB path is working.

## Requirements
- Expose qmd lookup from the local GPU Mac through a controlled mcp2cli/qmd wrapper or equivalent MCP bridge.
- Document trusted host and identity assumptions.
- Make failure behavior explicit and non-fatal for Hermes memory correctness.
- Do not make Hermes startup, recall, writes, current memory, or repo facts depend on qmd availability.
- Keep Open Brain as the required distributed memory/fact layer.

## Current Evidence
- Local qmd is healthy on the GPU Mac: `mcp2cli qmd status` reports collection `king` with 3,627 docs, `needsEmbedding: 0`, and vector index enabled.
- GPU-less Bilby can retrieve qmd-promoted King repo facts from Open Brain and follow the GitHub source pointer without qmd.
- Hosted mcp2cli and Hermes runtime no longer expose Honcho/local-memory fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Remote qmd wrapper is available as an explicitly optional deep lookup tool.
- Docs say it is not part of the Open Brain/Hermes memory contract.
- Failure of the wrapper degrades only deep lookup, not normal memory behavior.
